label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
output:
@Deirdre Fortuin thank you for asking me, and not just telling me. It means a lot.

I'm not going to fight this. I understand it's about the numbers, and Bronwyn needs the help more with 24 little ones. But I don't want to pretend I'm fine either. Noma has been in the Seahorses with me for three years, since my very first year teaching. She basically taught me how to do the sign-in sheets and the parent WhatsApp group without losing my mind. She does the isiXhosa songs at morning ring, and the kids ask for "Noma's song" every single day. When Zayd was struggling in Term 2, she was the only one who could calm him, sitting with him under the jungle gym. That's hard to replace, and I'll miss her.

What worries me is that the first weeks of Grade R are the hardest. New kids crying at the gate, and a new assistant on top of that, is a lot at once. So I'd love it if you could put two things to SMT:

1. **Handover days in December:** Could Charlene come in for a day or two in the last week of term (1 to 4 Dec) to meet Noma and see our routine in action? That way she isn't starting from scratch on 11 Jan.

2. **Morning ring in January:** Could Noma pop in for morning ring in the first week back, from 14 Jan, even just 15 minutes? Two of next year's kids, Luthando and Mia, already know her from aftercare, so a familiar face at the start would help them and the others settle. It would also be a nice way for Charlene to see how the songs and routines work.

It helps that Noma will still be just across the courtyard. I'm happy to work around whatever suits Bronwyn's class so it doesn't take Noma away from her.

Thanks again, Deirdre.
